1	# The page's date on the live read, and the first day of a live store: design for the council (D573; round 46), 2026-11-16, $0
     2	
     3	## A. The page opens on the served snapshot's day (built)
     4	
     5	**Defect** (`SERVING-WHILE-WRITING-RESULT.md`, finding 2): at start the page shows its embedded snapshot, then replaces it with the
     6	served library (`bootstrap.loadLibrary` → `library.setDataset`), whose clamp keeps the embedded day. A shell built on one day and opened
     7	on a later one therefore shows the shell's day, not the latest completed day. `thesis-ui.md`: "The supplied snapshot defines the
     8	displayed date."
     9	
    10	**Rule:** on the **first successful automatic read** only, the library shows the served snapshot's `as_of`, unless the person changed
    11	the date while the read was in flight (then their choice is kept, clamped as today). Every later replacement keeps today's verified
    12	clamp (`verify-library.mjs`, "library day clamps before replacement"). A failed read keeps the embedded snapshot, as the specification
    13	says ("Automatic API loading keeps the current snapshot when unavailable").
    14	
    15	**Owner:** `components/library.js` gains `setDataset(input, { day })` (a supplied day, clamped to the new history; without it, today's
    16	behaviour) and records whether the person has changed the date (`userChangedDay`); `bootstrap.loadLibrary` passes `{ day: next.as_of }`
    17	when `!library.userChangedDay()`. `thesis-ui.md` says it.
    18	
    19	**Proof ($0):** a unit or browser test of `setDataset` with and without `{ day }`; the existing clamp check unchanged; the paused-writer
    20	test re-run with the page check asserting the displayed day and the question identities against the served response (not only a
    21	count); a delayed-response case in which the person changes the date before the read returns (their date kept); the production shell

1	# Hivemind service: a thesis database with search
     2	
     3	D76, October 24, 2026; English edition and current-document refresh, October 25 (D163). Alex defined Hivemind as a database with a search engine on top. Its read service lets an agent or page find theses, choose what to use and inspect the state, history and evidence. Hivemind stores shared **theses**, not user ideas, positions or commitments. This distinction replaces the ambiguous use of “thesis” for both in the earlier document. The [historical source](../research/2026-10-25-english/service.original.md) retains prior wording and verification details.
     4	
     5	The core read service does not choose or arrange results for a caller. The separate [`POST /ideas` application flow](idea-card.md) discovers candidate theses, then adopts and weights them in a final assessment. The default `poc-v118-idea` configuration uses two discovery calls and one final assessment; older configurations retain their own contracts. The Idea specification owns those steps and their response. The route returns a UI-ready response.
     6	
     7	## Historical visibility
     8	
     9	Readers accept an `as_of` calendar day, defaulting to the ledger's last completed day. They do not use today's clock to reinterpret history. A row is visible when its dispatch sequence belongs to an item or daily round dated on or before that day. This applies to theses, switches, judgements, evidence links, sources, replacements, dependencies and resolutions. `history` and `changes` use explicit date spans.
    10	
    11	The historical sealed-ledger check found 28 dependency rows and 750 source rows newer than the theses/judgements they attach to; those rows must stay hidden in earlier reads. A later quotation or relationship must not appear in an old snapshot.
    12	
    13	## Interfaces and readers
    14	
    15	Field and route names are compatibility identifiers; `view` in an API name means the glossary's **thesis**.
    16	
    17	| Interface | Returned content | Reader |
    18	|---|---|---|
    19	| `search(query, k, as_of, include_closed)` | Query/day, semantic or lexical mode, missing current vectors, ranked results or null; each result includes ID, subject, kind, focus, question, due date, lifecycle, relationships and score components | Caller chooses relevant theses; search evaluation |
    20	| `views(object, as_of, include_closed)` | Thesis records | Agent or page |
    21	| `view(view_id, as_of)` | Identity, source, dates, ladder, current state or null, dependencies, dependants and counts | Agent or detail panel |
    22	| `history(view_id, from_day, to_day)` | Judgements, rung changes, evidence arrivals, replacements and lifecycle switches | History chart and replay |
    23	| `evidence(view_id, as_of, tier)` | Evidence in force, original quotes, summaries, tiers, speakers, dates and sources | Agent or evidence list |
    24	| `record(view_id, as_of)` | Last completed check with day/round and processed/arriving counts, or null | “Last checked” display |
    25	| `changes(since_day, to_day)` | Changed judgements with previous/current positions, reasons and historically visible citations | Polling agent |
    26	| `evaluate(view_id, comparator, value_usd, as_of)` | Whether evaluable and why; otherwise claim position, judged position/label/condition and verdict | Numeric claim display |
    27	| `thesis_bundles(view_ids, as_of)` / `GET /thesis-bundles?ids=...` | Complete dated bundles with ladder, judgements, historical evidence, sources, dependencies and switches | `fromBundles` in the modular UI |
    28	| `thesis_library(as_of)` / `GET /library?as_of=...` | Complete dated library and research groups under the [library envelope](#current-library-envelope-d275) | Library UI and agents |
    29	| `POST /ideas` | Idea, search summary, mapped parts and chosen theses, related theses, evaluation, optional bundles, days, trace and cost | Idea application/UI; see its contract |
    30	| Derived index | Content hashes, embedding model, vectors, token counts and build timestamps | Search only; not the thesis ledger |
    31	
    32	The service returns stored prose as stored. D275 points the read-service defaults at the collected English Jev library and its matching items database, with a separate derived-index directory. Explicit old-ledger paths remain supported. This changes neither matching semantics nor the configured Idea prompt.
    33	
    34	## Numeric claim evaluation
    35	
    36	Use structured numeric rung bounds where supplied; the legacy path parses text. Bounds must form an unbroken, non-overlapping partition. Each shared boundary belongs to exactly one band; a lowest money range may begin at zero. A non-money or unparseable ladder returns `evaluable: false` with a reason.
    37	
    38	Legacy parsing recognises comparator phrases, ranges, postfix bounds and exact amounts. It follows the clauses specifying the amount, ignoring preceding datelines and later remarks. A bare nonzero number is not automatically money; percentages, gigawatts and years are not dollar amounts. Chinese magnitude units remain accepted input. For example, 269.79 hundred-million dollars is exactly $26,979,000,000. The original-language regression strings remain in tests and the historical source document.
    39	
    40	The evaluation asks whether every amount in the judged band satisfies the user's claim (`holds`), none does (`not_yet`), or only some do (`borderline`). An equality claim holds only for a singleton amount. Missing judgement returns `not_judged`; an unassigned boundary is not guessed.
    41	
    42	Historical validation covered all 43 money ladders selected independently by text pattern and refused six non-money ladders. Boundary, exact-amount and dateline cases remain regression requirements. That result does not validate newly translated English-only bands; D163 must test those separately.
    43	
    44	## Search contract
    45	
    46	The index embeds each thesis's own text, not its evidence. A content hash detects outdated vectors. Search can report semantic mode only when all relevant candidates have usable current vectors; absent, empty or stale vectors require lexical mode and explicit missing-vector reporting. A second unchanged index build embeds nothing. A failed batch reports already stored progress.
    47	
    48	D91's null means no recorded coverage, not low relevance. D132 checks named subjects using IDs, full names and configured aliases (including products), the text index, and semantic coverage where enabled. An off-subject similarity floor is not a universal relevance threshold: an irrelevant sentence naming NVDA can score above a relevant narrower query. The caller still judges relevance.
    49	
    50	`--lexical` disables embedding calls throughout startup and requests. Query vectors are cached by text and model. The historical evaluation checks four example questions within their top three accepted matches, plus day-zero coverage; mapper suggestions are not human gold labels.
    51	
    52	## State × event and failures
    53	
    54	| State/event | Required behavior |
    55	|---|---|
    56	| Historical read | Filter every attached value by its own sequence/day, not only the thesis creation date |
    57	| Missing thesis | HTTP 404 or MCP tool error |
    58	| Invalid parameter | HTTP 400 |
    59	| Corrupt judgement | Raise `LedgerError`; HTTP 500, not fabricated state |
    60	| Missing/stale vector | Truthful lexical mode and missing-vector list |
    61	| Lexical configuration | No embedder invocation |
    62	| Read request | No ledger writes; derived index/cache writes remain separate |
    63	| Concurrent HTTP requests | Each request owns its SQLite connections |
    64	| Embedding failure | Report status/type without exposing the response body or credentials |
    65	
    66	No query opens, closes or rejudges a thesis. No read route stores user commitments or performs trades. The ingestion pipeline remains the ledger writer.
    67	
    68	## Transports and local operation
    69	
    70	- `scripts/hivemind_mcp.py` exposes the readers as tools over stdio or streamable HTTP at `/mcp`.
    71	- `scripts/hivemind_api.py` is the threaded HTTP front, listening on localhost by default.
    72	- Both build required index content at startup unless lexical mode is selected.
    73	- `Dockerfile`, `Dockerfile.mcp` and `docker-compose.yml` mount the ledger/items read-only and service index/archive storage read-write. Credentials remain server-side and are never included in a bundle.
    74	
    75	The October 24 environment check found both containers could answer local HTTP/MCP reads, but the host VPN did not carry Docker VM traffic for external model calls. The recorded options were host networking or an explicitly configured reachable proxy. This is an environment observation, not a current connectivity claim or authorisation to change networking.
    76	
    77	The [README](../../README.md#run-the-service-for-testing) owns executable startup and shutdown instructions. The HTTP default is port 8788. MCP defaults to stdio; port 8789 serves `/mcp` only when streamable HTTP is selected. Use `--lexical --config ''` on the HTTP front for reads without model calls; MCP's read-only tool set needs only `--lexical`. Local source databases are required and are not included in a clone.
    78	
    79	Verification requirements live in `tests/test_service.py`, `tests/test_search.py` and transport/bundle tests. New language behavior must retain their historical visibility, numeric, cache and failure guarantees. The [UI integration](../../poc/ui/README.md) documents the rendering boundary.
    80	
    81	## Current library envelope (D275)
    82	
    83	`GET /library?as_of=YYYY-MM-DD` and MCP `thesis_library` return all dated theses, including closed ones, and stored research groups. They call the same read-only bundle writer as `GET /thesis-bundles` / MCP `thesis_bundles`. The complete read is pinned in SQLite read transactions. No search, model call or ledger write occurs. HTTP bundle/library requests do not open an index or model archive.
    84	
    85	The envelope declares `coverage: library` or `coverage: selection`. Group members refer only to theses included in that envelope. Identity fields, all evidence source records, replacement recording dates, dependency resolution history and succession are projected from their existing tables. The UI adapts this into its [versioned contract](../../poc/ui/README.md). Original publication and recording dates are separate; membership and relationship visibility follow recording dates.

item.text:
**No-go as written.** The startup-date correction is appropriate, but the design assumes a date interaction the library does not currently expose. The first-day finding also remains an open defect; a documented operating rule alone does not make the service refuse the state the test exposed.

For **A**, `createLibrary` has `getDay` and `setDataset`, but no date picker, `setDay` or other person-driven change to its date. The explorer has a separate date control. The proposed `userChangedDay` flag therefore has no identified event to record, and the delayed-response test has no specified user action on the library. Trace the actual interaction to preserve—if there is none, simplify A to set the served day on the initial successful library load and keep the existing clamp for later replacements. [library.js](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/ui/src/components/library.js:12), [explorer](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/ui/src/index.js:78)

For **B**, the reader inventory is useful and confirms that changing `default_as_of` needs more design. But the proposed instruction to serve only after `/days` reports a completed day is not enforced by either service entry point. A crash can also leave a first-day partial store in that state longer than the design’s “only … to the end of its first day” implies. Record the restriction and the defect honestly; if it is the intended protection for the serving path, specify **who checks it, when, and how a failed check prevents serving**, with a real-entry-point test. A failed automatic page read currently retains the embedded snapshot silently, so that outcome remains a separately stated limitation. [LIVE-READ-DESIGN.md](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/page-contract/LIVE-READ-DESIGN.md:24), [bootstrap.js](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/ui/src/bootstrap.js:246)

The next step is to revise those two contracts, then run the planned paused-writer proof. The census and the existing completed-day checks are useful evidence; neither proves the first-day state safe to serve.

CONSENSUS: no, because A’s user-date-change path is not identified and B’s operating rule does not prevent the observed partial-day read.
